                    text: [32m'# Understanding GraphQL Mutations\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2019-04-04, last updated: 2026-05-05, [Read more](https://dev.to/eveporcello/understanding-graphql-mutations-52nl)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m''[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Changing data with GraphQL operations\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-16, [Read more](https://www.apollographql.com/tutorials/intro-dgs/12-mutations)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We declare the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type using the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m". Inside the curly braces, we have our entry points, the fields we'll be using to mutate our data.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For the fields of the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m', we recommend starting with a verb that describes the specific action of our update operation (such as\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'create\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Return types for\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Mutation\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'fields usually start with the name of the mutation, followed by\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Payload\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Mutations are write operations used to modify data.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Naming mutations usually starts with a verb that describes the action, such as "add," "delete," or "create."\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- It's a common convention to create a consistent response type for mutation responses.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'- Mutations in GraphQL often require multiple arguments to perform actions.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To group arguments together, we use a GraphQL input type for clarity and maintainability.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Mutations - GraphQL\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-30, [Read more](https://graphql.org/learn/mutations/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'GraphQL is similar—technically any field resolver could be implemented to cause a data write—but the GraphQL specification states that “the resolution of fields other than top-level mutation fields must always be side effect-free and idempotent.”\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Thus, for any spec-compliant GraphQL schemas, only the top-level fields in mutation operations are allowed to cause side effects.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A mutation can contain multiple fields, just like a query.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**While query fields are executed in parallel, mutation fields run in series.**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Serial execution of these top-level fields means that if we send two `deleteStarship` mutations in one request, the first is guaranteed to finish before the second begins, ensuring that we don’t end up in a race condition with ourselves.'[39m
                  }

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Parameters - EdgeQL | Reference\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-04-14, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/reference/edgeql/parameters)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Allow passing tuples as arguments · Issue #2326 · geldata/gel\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2021-03-05, last updated: 2025-05-02, [Read more](https://github.com/edgedb/edgedb/issues/2326)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m`We currently prohibit passing tuples as arguments, because Postgres doesn't support them either ("input of anonymous composite types is not implemented").\n`[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The basic strategy is to decompose an array of tuples into multiple parameters that take arrays of scalars.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In the case of multiply nested arrays, we produce fully flattened arrays of all of the scalars that appear in them and introduce an extra array<int64> parameter that indicates how the flattened arrays get associated into arrays.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The key technique is to decompose a tuple parameter into multiple\n'[39m +
                      [32m'parameters, one for each scalar component.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Arrays of tuples are\n'[39m +
                      [32m'essentially transposed into a tuple of arrays, and then decomposed.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Nested arrays are handled by flattening the array and adding an\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`array<int32>` parameter that stores the start/end of each subarray.'[39m

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A type cast expression converts the specified value to another value of\n'[39m +
                      [32m'the specified type:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"<" type ">" expression\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"*Implicit casts* happen automatically whenever the value type doesn't match the expected type in an expression.\n"[39m +
                      [32m"This is mostly supported for numeric casts that don't incur any potential information loss (in form of truncation), so typically from a less precise type, to a more precise one.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If *implicit* casting is supported for a given pair of types, *assignment* and *explicit* casting of those types is also supported.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `<>` - can be cast explicitly\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `:=` - assignment cast is supported\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `impl` - implicit cast is supported\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `*`- When casting a float type to an integer type, the fractional value\n'[39m +
                      [32m'naturally cannot be preserved after the cast.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When executing this cast, we'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Arrays - Standard Library | Reference\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-05-29, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/reference/stdlib/array)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|array[i]|Accesses the array element at a given index.|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|array[from:to]|Produces a sub-array from an existing array.|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|array ++ array|Concatenates two arrays of the same type into one.|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Arrays store expressions of the *same type* in an ordered list.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'An array constructor is an expression that consists of a sequence of\n'[39m +
                      [32m'comma-separated expressions *of the same type* enclosed in square brackets.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It produces an array value:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"[" expr [, ...] "]"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'array\n'[39m +
                      [32m'An ordered list of values of the same type.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Array indexing starts at zero.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'An array can contain any type except another array.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In Gel, arrays are\n'[39m +
                      [32m'always one-dimensional.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'std::array_agg(s: set of anytype) -> array<anytype>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Returns an array made from all of the input set elements.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'std::array_get(array: array<anytype>, index: int64, named only default: anytype = {} ) -> optional anytype\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Returns the element of a given *array* at the specified *index*.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'std::array_unpack(array: array<anytype>) -> set of anytype\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Returns the elements of an array as a set.'[39m

                [32m'**Validating Mutation Rewrites**\n'[39m +

                      [32m'created: 2023-03-07, last updated: 2026-07-24, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/reference/datamodel/triggers)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Triggers allow you to define an expression to be executed whenever a given\n'[39m +
                      [32m'query type is run on an object type.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The original query will *trigger* your pre-defined expression to run in a transaction along with the original query.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'If you need to modify the object, you can use mutation rewrites.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Triggers may also be used for validation by calling `assert()` inside the trigger.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'type type-name "{"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'trigger name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'after\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{insert | update | delete} [, ...]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    for {each | all}\n'[39m +

                      [32m'"}"\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Optionally provide a condition for the trigger.\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Triggers - Schema | Reference\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-03-07, last updated: 2026-07-24, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/reference/datamodel/triggers)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Triggers allow you to define an expression to be executed whenever a given\n'[39m +
                      [32m'query type is run on an object type.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The original query will *trigger* your pre-defined expression to run in a transaction along with the original query.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'These can be defined in your schema.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Triggers cannot be used to *modify* the object that set off the trigger, although they can be used with `assert()` to do *validation* on that object.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Triggers may also be used for validation by calling `assert()` inside the trigger.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'trigger name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'after\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{insert | update | delete} [, ...]\n'[39m +

                      [32m'do expr\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"}"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Triggers - Schema | Reference\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-03-07, last updated: 2026-07-24, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/reference/datamodel/triggers)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Syntax ​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type type-name "{"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'trigger name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'after\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{insert | update | delete} [, ...]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    for {each | all}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[ when (condition) ]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'do expr\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"}"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **each**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The expression will be evaluated once per modified object.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`__new__` and `__old__` in this context within the expression will refer to a single object.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **all**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The expression will be evaluted once for the entire query, even if multiple objects were modified.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`__new__` and `__old__` in this context within the expression refer to sets of the modified objects.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Added in v4.0- **when (condition)**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **expr**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The expression to be evaluated when the trigger is invoked.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The trigger name must be distinct from that of any existing trigger\n'[39m +
                      [32m'on the same type.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Define a new trigger.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{create | alter} type type-name "{"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'create trigger name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'after\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{insert | update | delete} [, ...]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    for {each | all}\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# ROW_COUNT\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2025-02-18, [Read more](https://www.firebirdsql.org/refdocs/langrefupd20-row_count.html)\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Returning A Row When Your Query Has No Results\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-04-10, last updated: 2026-07-07, [Read more](https://erikdarling.com/returning-a-row-when-your-query-has-no-results/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This is fairly obvious and straightforward.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You do the insert, check the row count, and return a message if it’s zero:\n'[39m +
                      [32m"> DECLARE @t table ( database_id integer, database_name sysname ); INSERT @t ( database_id, database_name ) SELECT d.database_id, d.name FROM sys.databases AS d WHERE d.database_id > 32767; IF @@ROWCOUNT > 0 BEGIN SELECT t.* FROM @t AS t; END; ELSE BEGIN SELECT msg = 'table @t is empty!'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'END;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In this case, you can use a common table expression in a rather handy way.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"> WITH d AS ( SELECT d.database_id, d.name FROM sys.databases AS d WHERE d.database_id > 32766 ) SELECT d.* FROM d UNION ALL SELECT 0, 'table @t is empty!'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'WHERE NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1/0 FROM d AS d2 );\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'left outer join sys.databases as d\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When I want to return at least 1 row from a query, I add the following lines to the main query.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It does require that you change the Where clause in the query to an ON clause of this join.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'ON {move the original WHERE clause here}'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Check if a SQL Select statement returns no rows\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2011-10-28, last updated: 2026-03-22, [Read more](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/7931984/check-if-a-sql-select-statement-returns-no-rows)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To find out whether no matching rows exist you can use `NOT EXISTS`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Which can be more efficient than counting all matching rows\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'IF NOT EXISTS(SELECT * FROM ...)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'BEGIN\n'[39m +
                      [32m"PRINT 'No matching row exists'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'END\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If this is SQL Server, try @@ROWCOUNT.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can use @@ROWCOUNT.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For e.g.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'SELECT QBalance\n'[39m +
                      [32m'FROM dbo.CustomerBalance\n'[39m +
                      [32m'WHERE (CustomerID = 1) AND (MarchentID = @MerchantId)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'--This will return no of rows returned by above statement.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'SELECT @@ROWCOUNT\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You will get 0 if first statement will not return any rows.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can also use if statement to check that just after first statement.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'e.g.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'IF @@ROWCOUNT <> 0\n'[39m +
                      [32m"PRINT 'Select statement is returning some rows'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'ELSE\n'[39m +
                      [32m"PRINT 'No rows returned'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"SELECT ISNULL(QBalance, 'ReplaceValue')\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Could also use an outer ISNULL check?\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'SELECT ISNULL((\n'[39m +
                      [32m'SELECT QBalance\n'[39m +
                      [32m'FROM dbo.CustomerBalance\n'[39m +
                      [32m'WHERE (CustomerID = 1) AND (MarchentID = @MerchantId)), 0)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Simple check for SELECT query empty result\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2010-05-21, last updated: 2026-03-20, [Read more](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/2884996/simple-check-for-select-query-empty-result)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'IF EXISTS(SELECT * FROM service s WHERE s.service_id = ?)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'BEGIN\n'[39m +
                      [32m'--DO STUFF HERE\n'[39m +
                      [32m'END\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Use @@ROWCOUNT:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'SELECT * FROM service s WHERE s.service_id = ?;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'IF @@ROWCOUNT > 0\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'SELECT * FROM service s WHERE s.service_id = ?;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'IF @@rowcount = 0\n'[39m +
                      [32m'begin\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# SET ROWCOUNT (Transact-SQL) - SQL Server - Microsoft Learn\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-11-18, last updated: 2025-11-26, [Read more](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/set-rowcount-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver17)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Causes SQL Server to stop processing the query after the specified number of rows are returned.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'SET ROWCOUNT { number | @number_var }\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Triggers - Schema | Reference\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-03-07, last updated: 2026-07-24, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/reference/datamodel/triggers)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Triggers allow you to define an expression to be executed whenever a given\n'[39m +
                      [32m'query type is run on an object type.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Syntax ​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type type-name "{"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'trigger name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'after\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{insert | update | delete} [, ...]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    for {each | all}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[ when (condition) ]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'do expr\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"}"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **all**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The expression will be evaluted once for the entire query, even if multiple objects were modified.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`__new__` and `__old__` in this context within the expression refer to sets of the modified objects.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Added in v4.0- **when (condition)**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Optionally provide a condition for the trigger.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If the condition is met, the trigger will run.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If not, the trigger is skipped.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **expr**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The expression to be evaluated when the trigger is invoked.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'on the same type.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Define a new trigger.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{create | alter} type type-name "{"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'create trigger name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'after\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{insert | update | delete} [, ...]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    for {each | all}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[ when (condition) ]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'do expr\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"}"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m

                    text: [32m'# For - EdgeQL | Reference | Gel Docs\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'With the help of a ``with`` block, we can add filters, ordering, and\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pagination clauses.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'``select``--retrieve or compute a set of values.\n'[39m +

Every `update` that changes `price_cents` appends the new price to the array; an `update` that leaves `price_cents` at its current value must leave the array untouched.  The 8 products that already exist must be backfilled with `revision = 1` and `price_history = []` (do not synthesize history for them).  ### 2. `default::AuditEvent` ??? one append-only row per audited row change  Properties:  - `action: str`, required, restricted to exactly the values `insert`, `update`, `delete`. - `sku: str`, required. - `old_price_cents: int64`, optional. - `new_price_cents: int64`, optional. - `recorded_at: datetime`, required, defaulting to the time of the statement that created it. - `summary: str`, required, and **always derived by the database from the other properties of the same object when the row is inserted** (a caller-supplied value must never survive). Exact formats:   - `action = 'insert'` ??? `INSERT <sku> price=<new_price_cents>`   - `action = 'update'` ??? `UPDATE <sku> price=<old_price_cents>-><new_price_cents>`   - `action = 'delete'` ??? `DELETE <sku> price=<old_price_cents>`  The type is append-only: inserting is allowed (including directly, by hand), but any attempt to `update` or `delete` an `AuditEvent` must fail with an error whose message contains exactly `AuditEvent is append-only`, and must leave the stored rows unchanged.  ### 3. `default::AuditBatch` ??? one row per mutating statement  Properties: `kind: str` (required, restricted to exactly `insert`, `update`, `delete`), `row_count: int64` (required), `recorded_at: datetime` (required, defaulting to the time of the statement that created it). It always performs the update, even when `<new_price_cents>` equals the current price, and it must run exactly one mutating statement per invocation. - Validation, applied strictly in this order, printing nothing to stdout and leaving the database untouched:   1. wrong number of arguments ??? stderr `ERROR: usage: apply_price_change.sh <sku> <new_price_cents>`, exit `4`.   2. `<new_price_cents>` is not a positive decimal integer (no sign, no leading zero, no decimal point) ??? stderr `ERROR: invalid price: <the argument as given>`, exit `3`.   3. no product with that `sku` ??? stderr `ERROR: unknown sku: <sku>`, exit `2`.  `scripts/audit_report.sh` ??? takes no arguments, always exits `0`, and prints a single JSON array to stdout (whitespace and line breaks inside the JSON do not matter). It contains one object per distinct `sku` that appears in `AuditEvent` ??? a sku with no audit rows must not appear at all, and an empty audit trail must yield `[]`. Objects are ordered by `sku` ascending and have exactly these six keys:  - `sku` (string) - `inserts`, `updates`, `deletes` (integers): number of `AuditEvent` rows for that sku with the corresponding `action` - `events` (integer): total number of `AuditEvent` rows for that sku - `net_price_change_cents` (integer): sum of `new_price_cents - old_price_cents` over that sku's `update` rows, `0` when there are none  ## Implementation Hints  - Project path: `/home/user/pricing-audit` (the `gel.toml` and `dbschema/` live there). - Commands: `/home/user/pricing-audit/scripts/apply_price_change.sh <sku> <new_price_cents>` and `/home/user/pricing-audit/scripts/audit_report.sh`.             [32m'  - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, use a single executeCommand call with \'&&\' to chain them together (e.g., `git add . && git commit -m "message" && git push`). For instance, if one operation must complete before another starts (like mkdir before cp, Write before executeCommand for git operations, or git add before git commit), run these operations sequentially instead.\n'[39m +
            [32m"  - Use ';' only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail\n"[39m +
            [32m'  - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings)\n'[39m +
            [32m"- You shall avoid use the markdown code block syntax (backtick, '`') in your command, as it will be interpreted as a command substitution.\n"[39m +

You must also consider if the command you need to run should be executed in a specific directory rather than the current working directory, and properly set the `cwd` if necessary.\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m"- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it\n'[39m +
            [32m'- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen  — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +
            [32m'- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the executeCommand tool:\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.\n'[39m +

            [32m"  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.\n"[39m +
            [32m'2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.\n'[39m +
            [32m'   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.\n'[39m +
            [32m'4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook changes, retry the commit ONCE to include these automated changes. If it fails again, it usually means a pre-commit hook is preventing the commit. If the commit succeeds but you notice that files were modified by the pre-commit hook, you MUST amend your commit to include them.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Important notes:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +

            [32m'- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so\n'[39m +
            [32m'- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.\n'[39m +
            [32m'- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Creating pull requests\n'[39m +
